# FsMcp 2.0 — Full LLM Context

FsMcp is an idiomatic F# layer over the official Microsoft
ModelContextProtocol .NET SDK. Version 2.0 targets .NET 10 and intentionally
corrects several public 1.x claims that were not connected to the SDK runtime.

Canonical documentation: https://neftedollar.com/FsMcp/
Repository: https://github.com/Neftedollar/FsMcp
Packages: https://www.nuget.org/packages?q=FsMcp

## Author

- [Roman Melnikov (Neftedollar)](https://neftedollar.com/)

## Install

    dotnet add package FsMcp.Server
    dotnet add package FsMcp.Client
    dotnet add package FsMcp.Testing
    dotnet add package FsMcp.TaskApi
    dotnet add package FsMcp.Server.Http
    dotnet add package FsMcp.Sampling

## Minimal cancellable server

```fsharp
open FsMcp.Core
open FsMcp.Server

type GreetArgs = { name: string; greeting: string option }

let server = mcpServer {
    name "MyServer"
    version "1.0.0"

    tool (TypedTool.define<GreetArgs> "greet" "Greets" (fun args cancellationToken -> task {
        cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested()
        let greeting = args.greeting |> Option.defaultValue "Hello"
        return Ok [ Content.text $"{greeting}, {args.name}!" ]
    }) |> unwrapResult)
}

Server.run server |> fun pending -> pending.GetAwaiter().GetResult()
```

`mcpServer { }` declares protocol primitives only. There is no `useStdio` or
`useHttp` selector in 2.0. `Server.run` hosts stdio. The FsMcp.Server.Http
package provides Streamable HTTP and caller-owned ASP.NET Core composition.

## Primary handler contracts

```fsharp
ToolDefinition.Handler :
    Map<string, JsonElement>
    -> CancellationToken
    -> Task<Result<Content list, McpError>>

ResourceDefinition.Handler :
    Map<string, string>
    -> CancellationToken
    -> Task<Result<ResourceContents, McpError>>

PromptDefinition.Handler :
    Map<string, string>
    -> CancellationToken
    -> Task<Result<McpMessage list, McpError>>
```

The SDK request token is authoritative. Caller cancellation is rethrown with
the caller's token instead of being translated into a protocol/transport error.
Use `Handler.ignoreCancellation` only when the operation genuinely performs no
cancellable work.

Typed handlers use strict JSON for record fields. JSON strings such as `"42"`
or `"true"` are not coerced into numeric or Boolean fields. URI-template and
prompt string arguments retain their string projection.

## Client truth

`McpClient` exposes Task-first operations and `McpClientAsync` carries the
ambient F# async cancellation token into request and connection operations.
Disconnect waits for one shared, non-cancellable ownership-cleanup task.

`McpClient.readResource` returns
`Task<Result<ResourceContents list, McpError>>`: all resource contents from the
SDK response are preserved. List functions enumerate all SDK pages. Prompt
details preserve the declared argument contract.

Every SDK content block is converted or the request fails explicitly. FsMcp's
`Content` DU supports text, image, and embedded text/blob resources. Other SDK
block types fail explicitly instead of disappearing or changing meaning.

## Enterprise-managed authorization

FsMcp.Client includes a typed wrapper for the stable MCP Enterprise-Managed
Authorization ID-JAG profile:

1. caller supplies the signed-in user's current OIDC ID token;
2. the enterprise IdP performs RFC 8693 token exchange to an ID-JAG;
3. the MCP authorization server exchanges the ID-JAG under RFC 7523;
4. FsMcp attaches the resource-scoped Bearer token to one configured origin.

Configuration values are opaque and validated before network access. Production
constructors require HTTPS. Development constructors permit plain HTTP only on
loopback. The implementation disables redirects and cookies, rejects downgrade
and off-origin token or resource requests, bounds token responses to 1 MiB,
bounds replayable request bodies to 4 MiB, uses single-flight token acquisition,
honors cancellation/timeouts, redacts secrets, and retries at most once after a
401 with a refreshed token.

The ready-made flow uses `client_secret_post` when configured. It does not
implement `client_secret_basic`, `private_key_jwt`, SAML assertions, DPoP, mTLS
sender-constrained tokens, dynamic client registration, or token introspection.
With the pinned MCP SDK 1.4.1, authorization-server issuer paths or queries are
rejected because SDK RFC 8414 discovery cannot preserve them. An IdP token
endpoint may be supplied explicitly and is matched exactly.

Client EMA does not authenticate the MCP resource server. The HTTP host must
configure ASP.NET Core authentication and authorization and protect the mapped
MCP endpoint.

## Hosting and middleware

Register FsMcp into caller-owned dependency injection and continue configuring
the returned official SDK builder. Use official SDK request filters for
protocol-level interception. For HTTP, use ASP.NET Core middleware,
authentication, authorization, rate limits, and endpoint policy around MapMcp.

The 1.x `McpMiddleware` declarations were accepted but never invoked by the SDK
bridge. Non-empty legacy middleware now fails closed. `Middleware.compose`,
`ValidationMiddleware`, and the old telemetry middleware remain obsolete
compatibility surfaces, not runtime protection.

## Resource subscriptions

Streamable HTTP stateful mode advertises and implements resource subscriptions.
Subscription identifiers and errors are opaque public values. Notification
fan-out is bounded and cancellation-aware, failed sessions are evicted, and
disconnect cleanup removes session subscriptions.

Stateless HTTP omits the capability and rejects subscription requests. Do not
infer identity or authorization from the subscription registry; resource-server
authentication and policy remain host responsibilities.

## Sampling and other corrected surfaces

FsMcp.Sampling 2.0 provides domain types, request builders, and explicit test
helpers. `SamplingTool.define` fails closed because the 1.x path never reached
the connected client's request-scoped sampling primitive. Use the official SDK
primitive directly until FsMcp provides correctly wired runtime support.

`DynamicServer` and legacy contextual notification helpers likewise do not
claim hot-reload or notification behavior that the transport cannot honor.

## Testing

FsMcp.Testing invokes tool, resource, and prompt handlers directly. The
`callToolWithCancellation`, `readResourceWithCancellation`, and
`getPromptWithCancellation` variants prove token propagation. Convenience
variants use `CancellationToken.None`. Expecto assertions and FsCheck generators
cover domain values without requiring a transport.

## Release dependency policy

- exact .NET SDK: 10.0.400, roll-forward disabled
- ModelContextProtocol SDK: exact 1.4.1 through central MSBuild properties
- Microsoft.Extensions packages: exact 10.0.7 through central properties
- public FSharp.Core dependency floor: 10.1.203
- exact project lock files and locked restore
- SHA-pinned GitHub Actions
- seven-package closed-set pack/metadata/consumer verification
- NuGet vulnerability audit must be clean
- Docusaurus 3.10.2 is exact; npm permits only the reviewed two image-size
  denial-of-service advisories and their exact dependency closure through
  2026-09-30

## Breaking migration checklist

1. Add a final `CancellationToken` argument to every handler.
2. Handle all items returned by `McpClient.readResource`.
3. Remove `useStdio`, `useHttp`, and `ServerConfig.Transport`; select the runner.
4. Move middleware to SDK filters or ASP.NET Core.
5. Replace dynamic/contextual/sampling runtime assumptions with supported SDK
   primitives.
6. Treat subscription identifiers/errors as opaque and handle `Result` values.
7. Configure authentication/authorization on every HTTP resource server,
   including servers called by enterprise-authorized clients.
